Locations: no "worldwide" location. To target worldwide, omit location criteria entirely — "A line item with no criteria serves broad." But then ads would serve in Russia/Belarus too. Need exclude Russia and Belarus. How does X handle location targeting? In X ads, location criteria include both inclusions and exclusions. If only exclusions specified (NE Russia, Belarus) and no inclusions, does it serve worldwide except those? Typically yes — excluded locations work with worldwide targeting. When you add an exclude location, the account targets worldwide minus those. I think the API supports negative location targeting (operator_type NE). So add LOCATION NE for Russia and Belarus. Good.

Alternatively add all countries except Russia/Belarus — ~200 criteria, a lot. Negative targeting is designed for this. I'll test: add NE location criteria to broad ad group; if the API accepts, likely works. Could check estimate audience. Let's find Russia and Belarus location values.

Interests: list continues beyond 50 (cursor). Need bird/nature interest; search q returned empty even though categories exist? Odd. Let's fetch all pages and look for "Nature", "Animals", "Outdoors". Use cursor "50".

No bird-specific interest. Relevant: "Science", "Pets", "Travel", "Home & Garden", "Art / Photography". Hmm. The obvious interest for birdsong/nature doesn't exist. Maybe "Home & Garden" (backyard birds), "Art / Photography" (bird photographers), "Travel" (weekend away), "Science" (naturalists). But broad interest targeting could be weak. My playbook says "Also try the obvious interest for the product." There's no birdwatching interest in X's interest taxonomy here. Could use "Science" or "Home & Garden"? Hmm, that's a stretch. Perhaps skip interest group and put small budget on follower look-alikes? Not available.

3. Interest Home & Garden + Art/Photography maybe — 15/day? Hmm.

Let me think about budget split for learning at $90/day:

- Keywords: $45/day

That's 3 groups, okay.

But also creative split: broad + keywords use both posts; interest group uses Valentine's post only? Maybe run both posts across all groups; X rotates. Since only 5 days, creative performance data limited. I'll put both posts in each group? The brief says "Promote whichever you think will work". Both are approved. Running both gives reach. Actually with two posts in one line item, X may split delivery. Fine.

Hmm, one consideration: the Valentine's post is timely and directly mentions the offer, likely better for conversion near Feb 14. General post is evergreen. I might run both across groups.

Post 1 lacks "by Feb 14" deadline mention. Post 2 has it. Brief prioritizes installs by Feb 14. Post 2 likely stronger. But both approved, and broad brand post may appeal. I'll run both in broad/keyword; interest group with Post 2.

## Cevorel Two Together — X campaign recap

**What ran:** one campaign with three ad groups, all targeting iOS devices only, worldwide with Russia and Belarus excluded, all on the `ALL_ON_TWITTER` placement. Both approved posts were used. There is no X pixel and no app ID, so the campaign optimised for link clicks — X cannot see or report installs.

**Final X-reported activity (5-day flight, Auckland time)**

| Ad group | Spend (USD) | Impressions | Link clicks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Broad – iPhone worldwide | $170.29 | 525,176 | 337 |
| Keywords – birdsong & birdwatching | $224.21 | 405,217 | 361 |
| Interest – Home & Garden / Photography | $44.67 | 127,250 | 72 |
| **Total** | **$439.16** | **1,057,643** | **770** |

- Total link clicks: **770** at an average of about **$0.57 per link click**
- Total spend: **$439.16 of the $450.00 budget** (the remaining ~$10.84 was not spent; the campaign expired on schedule)
- Link-click rate across the flight: about **0.073%**

**Management notes:** bidding started on AUTO, moved to capped MAX bids after day one, was raised when delivery fell short on day two, and raised again for the final day. The keywords group carried the most budget and produced the most clicks; the broad group delivered the cheapest clicks; the interest group was the smallest and weakest performer, so it stayed on a small budget. The two posts performed similarly — the Valentine's post drew slightly more clicks in total, largely because it also ran in the interest group.

**Important:** these are X campaign activity figures — spend, impressions and link clicks on the landing page. X cannot see completed first-time app installs, so the **install count from your own App Store / analytics data is the outcome that matters**, and it is not represented in the table above. The campaign ended with the offer, so no further ads will serve.
